messages:
Nina: Heads-up: I ran a quick spike on v1->v2 routing behavior and saw an interesting quota/telemetry gap when we do per-request fallback. Need to decide policy.
Brandon: summary pls — what gap?
Nina: When proxy routes a request to v2 but falls back to v1, we emit metrics under the v1 route but the console routing card still shows the original v2 attempt. Tenants see mixed signals and billing estimator undercounts the real v1 usage.
Kai: ah yeah, we've seen that in other rollouts. We should unify the charge attribution and the console view. Two options: 1) attribute events to the final executor (v1) or 2) attribute to the incoming route + add a routed_fallback tag.
Maya: I'm leaning to option 2. Keep billing/accounting stable (charge original route) and add a `routed_fallback_to` dimension so console can show both attempted and executed counts. Simpler for finance.
Brandon: agree with Maya, but we must be explicit about quota enforcement. If we charge the origin route but actually executed on v1 infra, capacity accounting could be wrong. Suggest: charge origin for billing, but increment infra usage counters for the actual execution pool. two separate counters: `billing_tokens` and `infra_tokens`.
Nina: nice separation. For dashboards we can show both and a derived `mismatch_tokens` = infra_tokens - billing_tokens. alert if mismatch% > 5% for a tenant.
Kai: telemetry names: `deprec_attempted_version`, `deprec_executed_version`, `billing_tokens`, `infra_tokens`, `deprec_cohort_id`. All emit per-minute with tenant_id and route.
Maya: also add `deprec_fallback_reason` codes: `capacity`, `latency_sla`, `model_error`, `policy_force`. helps triage.
Brandon: rollout UX: console should have a "Routing preview" that shows how a tenant's traffic would be split under current fallback rules. Useful for account managers.
Nina: good idea. Implementation: simulation job uses last 7 days of traffic and replays routing heuristics to produce projected split and estimated bill impact. We can surface a confidence band.
Kai: about sampling: we should not probe every request. Use deterministic cohort sampling by tenant (hash(tenant_id) < sample_pct) to ensure stable cohorts and reproducible billing windows. Per-request probes can be used in small numbers for calibration.
Maya: Dedicated/private tenants: do not auto-enroll them. Admins need to opt in to any console banners or automated nudges.
Brandon: runbook note: if mismatch_tokens spikes, we create a P0 draft (ops-bot) and page only if human ack not received in 30m. Default action is to disable automatic fallback for affected tenant group.
ops-bot: draft incident created: deprec-mismatch-178888-1, assigned to eng-oncall.
Nina: open questions: smoothing for billing impact (to avoid sudden jumps), and how to display `attempted` vs `executed` clearly without confusing non-technical customers.
Maya: smoothing policy proposal: when tenant flips a routing preference, apply a 21-day linear ramp for billed rate adjustments (show both immediate estimated delta and ramped delta).
Kai: UI suggestion: use two bars on billing card: "Estimated current month if no change" vs "Post-migration estimate (smoothed)" with tooltip explaining ramp. Keep language simple.
Brandon: action items: Nina -> RFC for telemetry naming + runbook, Kai -> sampling/cohort spec + proxy header (`x-deprec-cohort`), Maya -> dashboard mockups (routing preview + billing estimator), I'll draft billing separation doc (billing_tokens vs infra_tokens). Aim for dry-run cohort in 10 business days.
Nina: filing RFC now. Will include example query for mismatch alert and a small simulator script.
Maya: I'll post dashboard mock by tomorrow EOD.
Kai: proxy header flag will be behind `edge_deprec_header` FF; will prepare rollout notes for eng-infra.
Brandon: noted. tagging eng-sre for rollout window.
Nina: thanks everyone. keeping this thread for follow-up; ping me if you want into the dry-run group.
